_doc: B0-D — the Li+Ln coordination cost/convergence probe. 🔴 RULES, not a typed-out list.
_why_rules_not_a_list: A hand-typed list of 19 and a rule that generates them are two sources of one truth, and this project has lost a round to that shape six times. The list is DERIVED (sei_pilot/b0_species.py) and PINNED by tests/test_b0_species.py, which asserts the exact id set and the count.
_ruling: lead relaying proposer5, 2026-08-19, TWICE. (1) 19 closed-shell species: bare Li+ IN, Li(PF6)3(2-) OUT. (2) 🔴 REVISED -- 19 -> 23: an OPEN-SHELL STRATUM was added because the 19 are ALL closed-shell singlets while HALF THE PRODUCTION POOL IS OPEN-SHELL. Every reduced species in S1/S2 is a radical, so B0-D as first specified sampled only the closed-shell half and could not see the failure mode most likely to bite production.
_n_note: n = 0 is the bare Li+ reference state. Multisets (mixed ligands included, order irrelevant) give 1 + 3 + 6 + 10 = 20 before exclusions.
_multiplicity_note: Li+ and all three ligands are closed-shell; every member of this set is a singlet. 🔴 This is NOT true of B0-F's species, which are doublet radicals -- see b0_reactions.json.

exclusions.reason: 🔴 EXCLUDED BY RULING (proposer5 via lead). Very likely NOT A BOUND SPECIES at this size. Its non-convergence would be a DIFFERENT failure from the one B0-D exists to measure, so including it would contaminate the u_cheap distribution with an artefact -- the C-10 conflation in a new place.
exclusions._not_deleted_because: 🔒 A removed option travelling without its removal reason is how this project lost two revisions (05_STATE's structural rule). The exclusion is recorded so nobody re-adds it as an oversight.

bound_species_rule._rule: 🔒 A COST/CONVERGENCE PROBE MUST CONTAIN ONLY BOUND SPECIES. An unbound species measures the BASIS SET, not the protocol.
bound_species_rule._ruling: lead relaying proposer5, 2026-08-19, generalised from the Li(PF6)2(-) instance.
bound_species_rule._diagnostic_note: The energy of the highest occupied orbital -- HOMO for a closed shell, SOMO for an open shell. A POSITIVE value means the electron is not bound and the 'orbital' is a discretised continuum state whose energy is a property of the basis set, not of the molecule. Free: it is in every log.
bound_species_rule._applies_to_note: 🟢 BROADENED BY RULING (proposer5, 2026-08-19), replacing the coder's `charge < 0`. proposer5 rejected its own earlier framing: `charge < 0` is a PROXY, and the property wanted is 'is the highest occupied orbital BOUND?'. 🔴 The classic unbound case in OUR chemistry is a RADICAL ANION -- gas-phase EC has a NEGATIVE adiabatic electron affinity, which is why ADR-029 insists on diffuse functions. Once the open-shell stratum lands we have NEUTRAL species whose SOMO boundness is the live question, and `charge < 0` WOULD SKIP EVERY ONE OF THEM. 🔒 The earlier note was labelled 'CODER EXTENSION, FLAGGED FOR CONFIRMATION'; that mechanism is what made this cheap to adjudicate and it is kept.

on_unbound._note: 🔴 'unbound' is a RESULT ABOUT THE SPECIES and is reported. It is NOT a convergence failure and must never be averaged into the convergence rate -- that would be the same conflation as counting a TRIPWIRE-ABORTED run as a chemical verdict.

open_shell_stratum._doc: 🔴 A STRATUM, not a bolt-on for B0-F. Open-shell SCF convergence is a distinct and well-known failure mode -- spin contamination, symmetry-broken solutions, multiple SCF minima -- and ADR-029 already recommends `stable=opt` for radical anions because of it. B0-D exists to answer 'how expensive and how convergent is this class?' and the closed-shell stratum alone cannot answer it for the half of production that is radicals.
open_shell_stratum._also_supplies: 🟢 endpoints for ALL THREE B0-F reactions. R-A/R-B's reactant is Li(EC)•, whose only existing geometry is the idealised li_ec_radical.xyz -- exactly the kind of guess that produced P1. R-C's reactant is Li(EC)2•. 'All three needed conformer-searched open-shell reactants regardless; R-C merely made it visible.'
open_shell_stratum._c8_is_satisfied_by_arm1: 🟢 arm 1 validates them: MTD -> opt -> DFT opt+freq, n_imag = 0. Nothing is special-cased. Arm 1 extends with `xtb --uhf 1`.

members._note: ALSO the reactant of B0-F R-A and R-B
ALSO the reactant of B0-F R-C, and production-sized

open_shell_stratum._reporting_rule: 🔴 u_cheap MUST be reported SEPARATELY for the closed- and open-shell strata. NEVER POOLED. 🟢 And the DIFFERENCE between them is itself a measurement we need -- 'does open-shell cost more and converge worse?' -- directly relevant to production, where half the pool is open-shell and NOTHING IN THE PLAN CURRENTLY MEASURES IT.

arm3._doc: r_high — the SAME species at the HIGH level, from ARM 1'S CONFORMER. Same start, and a start that is not pathological.
arm3._why_same_start: proposer5's correction to engineer5: 'same starting geometry' is not sufficient. If BOTH members start from the same IDEALISED geometry the measurement is the cost of climbing out of a bad guess at two levels -- which is exactly what produced li_ec_cation r_high = 0.38.
arm3._must_emit_frequency_list_why: 🔴 NOT just the energy. Arm 3 runs the same species at BOTH levels from the SAME conformer, which RESTORES THE CROSS-BASIS FREQUENCY COMPARISON that ADR-035 pre-registered and P1b lost (U-60: the reopen condition fired with an EMPTY result). Zero additional cost -- the frequencies are already computed.
arm3._honest_limit: ⚠ It compares REAL modes, not the IMAGINARY one the M2 window governs. Related evidence, not the identical measurement.
arm3._why_it_is_still_the_useful_case: 🔴 It is the HARDER case, which makes it MORE useful: low-frequency modes are the most basis-sensitive part of a Hessian. If they are stable across bases a stiffer imaginary mode very likely is too -- and if they are NOT, ADR-035's premise is refuted on the strongest available sample.
arm3._also_feeds: curvature.u55_panel — the three observables are computed from these same frequency lists at both levels, so the U-55 correlation gets a level axis free.
